answer: Divergent Challenge Ladder.** Each identity must answer a fresh, randomized challenge drawn from a shared pool; clones root at the same iteration and cannot fork without splitting. Passing demands sequential work along a unique derivation vine, so N clones pay N sequential costs rather than one shared. Colluding copies of one root collapse to a single branch, like a nebula with no scatter. The per-identity cost is full sequential work with no amortization; a legitimate oasis of one pays once, while a sybil farm pays linearly in identity count.
